intro: A straight path between a noise sample and a data sample has a time-dependent position but a constant target velocity. Flow matching trains a predictor against that velocity.
task: Return the interpolated points, target velocities and prediction loss. Inspect what changes with time and what stays fixed when the endpoints are held constant.
requirements: x0, x1 and predicted_velocity have the same nonempty shape (B,D). times is a vector of length B with entries in [0,1].
Compute point[b]=(1-times[b])*x0[b]+times[b]*x1[b] and velocity=x1-x0. Time zero is the noise endpoint x0; time one is the data endpoint x1.
Return a dictionary with point, velocity and loss. The first two are (B,D) arrays; loss is mean((predicted_velocity-velocity)**2) over all B*D elements. No model or sampling trajectory is executed.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Give time a feature axis
hints.body: A (B,1) time array broadcasts across each row without mixing examples.

hints.title: Differentiate the straight path
hints.body: The derivative with respect to time is x1-x0. The target is a velocity, not the current position.

explanation: Changing time moves the point along the segment, but it does not change the target velocity for fixed endpoints. A model prediction would usually depend on that point and time; here it is supplied explicitly.
The mean includes both the batch and feature axes. Summing feature errors before averaging the batch introduces an extra factor of D.
Adapted the upstream velocity MSE and added an inspectable straight-path interpolation. Inputs and outputs are NumPy arrays, and no trained generative model is implied.
